tasks.short: Set up and operate computer-controlled machines

steps.what: Set up workholding, tools and workpieces for the approved machine programme
Operate computer-controlled machines, prove the setup and attend machining conditions

tasks.design: Retain physical setup, proving and attendance at the {OTHER} machine controller. Existing programmed cycles already perform machining; their runtime is not operator labour and earns no new saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe setup requires physical checks of tools, workholding and actual conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability removes the hands-on work in this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected conditions, setup errors and safe first-piece proving.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when the actual machine differs from the planned setup.
tasks.altitude: No change to setup time, attendance or operating authority.

reach.task: Agree first-piece checks for the actual setup

evidence.claim: Retaining physical setup and attendance is an E1 design judgement; CAM preparation capabilities do not prove savings in these actions.

assumptions: Boundary is physical setup and operation, excluding programme preparation and transfer accounted in other tasks. Unattended cycle time is outside the human denominator.

Existing authorised programming produces the approved programme and setup instructions. The operator checks machine, tools, workholding, stock and programme identity in fully retained s1; absent instructions require manual clarification.
No automatic workholding, robotic loading or new sensor feed is assumed. Zero upkeep because no workflow change is introduced.
research_questions: What physical checks remain mandatory for each setup?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=50+50=100; gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Existing cycle runtime is not saved human labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review specifications and determine machine sequencing

steps.what: Review program specifications and blueprints and identify dimensions, tolerances and setup constraints
Determine machine operations and sequencing using the verified requirements
Check sequence feasibility and approve the setup plan for programme preparation

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} computer-aided manufacturing system's approved operation templates for repeat part features. The operator checks the drawing and requirements, selects applicable templates and approves the exact proposed sequence; unfamiliar features stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated operations and their parameters are recreated for similar parts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native feature recognition and operation libraries can populate an explicit draft sequence.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing viable workholding, access and order for an unusual part.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding drawing intent and whether the actual setup can make the part.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive sequencing entry; no new design or release authority.

reach.task: Resolve an unsupported feature or sequencing conflict
reach.learn: Operation template limits and simulation requirements

evidence.claim: NX CAM recognises features and applies standard operations; this supports native repeat-feature preparation rather than automatic release.
The operator time split and savings are E1 scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is requirements review and sequence planning, excluding programme editing, machine transfer and physical proving. Benefits overlapping programmer work must be assigned once.

Engineering supplies the released drawing and revision. The operator captures or verifies part revision, dimensions, tolerances, material, machine capability and workholding limits in fully retained s1.

In s2 the operator selects template identifiers and enters required feature parameters; this capture and applicability judgement stay in its 27 retained hours. Unsupported geometry or missing digital models require manual planning.
Test native feature recognition and operation libraries first. Templates only populate defined operations; the human chooses suitability. Local authority to approve a plan must be confirmed.
research_questions: How much sequence preparation remains after template selection and feasibility checks?

already_counted.description: Template selection, parameter capture and unsupported-feature handling
Final setup plan review and approval

incremental.description: Maintain approved operation templates and example checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact part revision, machine, workholding, operations, sequence and parameter set; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+45*0.60+20=82; gross=18, upkeep=3, net=15. High assumes repeat features; low assumes existing templates already cover the work and new upkeep yields no gross benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Listen for abnormal machine sounds and adjust operation

steps.what: Listen to machines and recognise dull-tool sounds or excessive vibration
Adjust machines within authorised limits and check whether the concern persists

tasks.design: Keep listening, diagnosis and authorised adjustments with the operator at the {OTHER} machine controller. No new acoustic sensor, validated classifier or automatic controller is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interpreting sound depends on tooling, workpiece and current cutting conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported software-only change removes these sensory and physical actions.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing normal variation from a dangerous or damaging condition.
tasks.human_edge: Experienced sensory recognition and prompt safe intervention.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring time and adjustment authority are unchanged.

reach.task: Escalate persistent vibration or an unsafe operating condition

evidence.claim: Keeping sensory fault recognition and corrective judgement human is an E1 design judgement; the digest gives no acoustic monitoring case.

assumptions: Boundary is live listening and authorised adjustment, excluding detailed maintenance and separately counted programme changes.
The operator produces observations in fully retained s1 and checks response in fully retained s2; no structured fault code is assumed.
Existing authorised setup instructions supply limits. Unclear limits or unresolved problems require stopping and escalation under local procedures.
Zero upkeep because no system or procedure change is introduced.
unknowns: Current monitoring requirements and adjustment limits
research_questions: Which sound changes require stopping rather than adjustment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=65+35=100; gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Listening and corrective actions remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Implement programme changes and enter specifications

steps.what: Confirm authorised changes, specifications and the target machine programme version
Edit machine programs and enter new specifications using approved parameter templates
Validate changes by comparison and simulation and approve the exact programme for transfer
Transfer the approved programme package to the specified machine controller

tasks.design: Configure parameter templates and controlled programme transfer in the {OTHER} computer-aided manufacturing and controller systems. The operator captures the change, checks edits and simulation, and approves a version-bound package before automatic staging; execution and first-piece proving remain separate human actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated parameter entry and manual file transfer add work around an authorised change.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and version-controlled transfer can reduce re-entry while preserving validation.
tasks.still_hard: An incorrect specification, postprocessor or actual setup can invalidate otherwise consistent code.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the change and recognising unsafe or unintended programme behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat entry and transfer; no automatic machining or expanded change authority.

reach.task: Resolve a change outside the approved parameter template

evidence.claim: Siemens states that CAM output requires programmer validation and simulation before NC code runs; this supports retained validation, not unsupervised execution.
Parameter-template reuse, controlled staging and task-specific savings are E1 proposals.

assumptions: Boundary covers authorised edits, validation and staging, excluding operation and first-piece proving counted in setup. Shared preparation benefits must be assigned once across tasks and roles.

The operator verifies or captures part revision, target machine, current programme version, changed fields, new values, units and authorised scope in fully retained s1. No structured change request is assumed without that capture.

S2 produces the programme file and revision. In fully retained s3 the operator checks specifications, simulation and the package hash, target controller, postprocessor version and approved transfer action; these become the structured transfer contract for s4.
S4 accepts only the exact hash and controller approved in s3; edits or target changes void approval. Failed transfer remains stopped and returns to the operator, covered by incremental exceptions.
Test native templates and transfer first. Transfer only stages a file and cannot start a machine, alter guards or bypass local proving requirements; unsupported changes remain manual.
research_questions: Do templates and staging reduce labour after full parameter and simulation checks?
Can the controller enforce exact-version transfer without starting execution?

already_counted.description: Parameter capture checks, edits and manual exceptions
Comparison, simulation and exact-version transfer approval

incremental.description: Maintain templates, transfer mappings, validation examples and failed-transfer handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact programme hash and revision, part revision, target controller, postprocessor and staging-only action; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+40*0.50+25+5*0=75; gross=25, upkeep=4, net=21. High assumes repeated parameter edits and manual transfer; low assumes unsupported changes leave only 4 gross hours offsetting upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical setup and condition monitoring remain human; approved templates may reduce repeat planning and programme-entry work.
reach: Agree first-piece requirements with quality control
role.ambitious_version: Use released preparation time for stronger setup and change verification, within existing operating authority.
